{"id": "32071e3a-ccd0-4a53-b0f2-5bd0a36c031c", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "What is the difference between an Application Load Balancer and a Network Load Balancer?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "f1d1fc3f-bfcd-4e8a-b13a-b16559e4454e", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "thinking", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "This is a general AWS conceptual question rather than something specific to the DevOps Agent product, so I can answer directly from stable knowledge without needing verification.\n\n"}]}

{"id": "254f0291-35a5-4000-a430-1c3f69e9eabd", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Both are Elastic Load Balancing types. They work at different network layers, which drives most of the differences.

| | **Application Load Balancer (ALB)** | **Network Load Balancer (NLB)** |
|---|---|---|
| **OSI layer** | Layer 7 (application) | Layer 4 (transport) |
| **Protocols** | HTTP, HTTPS, gRPC, WebSocket | TCP, UDP, TCP_UDP, TLS |
| **Routing** | Content-based: host, path, headers, query strings, HTTP method, source IP | Connection-based: protocol and port only |
| **Performance** | Good for web traffic, with request-level processing overhead | Very high throughput and ultra-low latency, and it handles sudden traffic spikes well |
| **Static IPs** | No. It uses DNS names, and its IPs can change. | Yes. It has one static IP per AZ and supports Elastic IPs. |
| **Client IP preservation** | Passed in the `X-Forwarded-For` header | Preserved natively at the network level for instance targets |
| **TLS** | Terminates TLS and offers SNI, certificate management, and authentication through Cognito or OIDC | Can terminate TLS or pass it through to targets |
| **Security groups** | Supported | Supported (added in 2023), but it's optional |
| **Target types** | Instances, IPs, Lambda functions | Instances, IPs, ALB |
| **Other features** | Redirects, fixed responses, weighted target groups, WAF integration | PrivateLink (VPC endpoint services) and long-lived connections |

**When to choose an ALB**
- You run HTTP/HTTPS web apps, APIs, or microservices.
- You need path-based or host-based routing, such as `/api` going to one service and `/images` to another.
- You need Lambda targets, WAF, or built-in user authentication.

**When to choose an NLB**
- You need extreme performance or very low latency, or you have millions of requests per second.
- You use non-HTTP protocols, such as gaming, IoT, VoIP, or custom TCP/UDP services.
- Clients or firewalls need fixed IP addresses to allow-list.
- You want to expose a service privately through AWS PrivateLink.

**Common pattern:** Put an NLB in front of an ALB (ALB-type target) when you want static IPs or PrivateLink along with Layer 7 routing.

I can also look at the load balancers in your AWS account and help you decide which fits a specific workload.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
